name: Western Australia Aboriginal Ranger Program

administered_by.name: Parks and Wildlife Service, Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA)

summary: Competitive grants to Aboriginal organisations that lead ranger programs caring for Country across Western Australia, including land and sea management, fire, weed and feral animal control and restoration work.

eligibility.rule: Is an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation (ACCO) as defined by Closing the Gap
Have legal right and/or access rights to undertake proposed activities on the land
Demonstrate cultural authority to access land and deliver proposed activities, with support letters where relevant
Undertake activities in Western Australia outside the Perth metropolitan region

documents: Letters of support from Prescribed Body Corporate, Regional Corporation or Traditional Owners, if required
Letters of support from all relevant landowners and land managers
Clearly marked map or aerial photograph
Ranger-related planning document, if applying to Sustain or Activate

status.quote: The ARP provides funding through competitive funding rounds. There are no rounds open at the moment.

applicant_types.quote: provides funding to Aboriginal organisations leading ranger programs through the allocation of competitive grants.

geography.quote: in regional and remote communities across Western Australia.

access.quote: The ARP provides funding through competitive funding rounds.

pool.quote: Round 9 begins Phase 3 investment by providing $62 million in funding to 34 ranger organisations across three different funds.

window.quote: The ARP provides funding through competitive funding rounds.

administered_by.quote: Administered by the Parks and Wildlife Service of the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions (DBCA)

co_finance_required.quote: Applicants are encouraged to seek other funding sources to complement any ARP funding and expand the potential outcomes of their project ideas, but it is not essential to being awarded ARP funding in this round.

consortium_required.quote: There may only be one applicant organisation per ranger project application.

effort.quote: The closing date for applications is 5.00pm AWST on Monday 9 March 2026. You are encouraged to submit your application in advance of this time and date to allow time for any unexpected technical issues which may arise. Applications can only be made by via the DBCA SmartyGrants online portal.
Eligible applications are provided to the Assessment Panel.

eligibility.quote: be an Aboriginal Community Controlled Organisation (ACCO) as defined by the National Agreement on Closing the Gap.
have a legal right and/or right to access and undertake the proposed activities on the land included in your application
demonstrate that you have cultural authority to access land and deliver the proposed activities (via appropriate letters of support, where relevant - see section 2.2.2)
Activities must be undertaken in Western Australia, but not within the Perth metropolitan region.

after_award.quote: You will need to report against these measures in your annual reports
Annual independently audited financial statements will be required for all agreements.

documents.quote: Letters of support from Prescribed Body Corporate (or equivalent), Regional Corporation or Traditional Owners, if required (refer to section 2.2.2 for more information); Letters of support from all relevant landowners and land managers (refer to section 2.2.3 for more information); Detailed project location information (refer to section 2.2.3 for more information)
a clearly marked map or aerial photograph
If you are applying in the Sustain or Activate Funds, attach your ranger related planning document/s.
